LESSON: METALS AND ALLOYS

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: INTEGRATED SCIENCE
Strand: Mixtures, Elements, and Compounds
Topic 1.2: Metals and Alloys

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Metals and Alloys
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: How are alloys important in day-to- day life?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. describe the physical properties of metals
2. describe the composition of alloys
3. identify the uses of metals and alloys in day-to-day life
4. explain the effects of rusting of metals
5. appreciate the importance of common alloys in day-to-day life

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Metals and Alloys

Teach
• Observe Metals and Alloys in real life (school compound, home, farm).
• Use safe examples only.
• Name → explain → apply.

Worked example
• Fact 1 about Metals and Alloys (in pupil words).
• Fact 2 with a Kenyan example.
• Safe action connected to Metals and Alloys.

Try this
• Draw/label one diagram for Metals and Alloys.
• Write 5 bullet facts about Metals and Alloys.
• Say one safety rule.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• describe the physical properties of metals
• describe the composition of alloys
• identify the uses of metals and alloys in day-to-day life

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. List 8 facts on Metals and Alloys.
2. Teach a friend using only bullet points.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet for Metals and Alloys: meaning, diagram, 5 practice questions.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How are alloys important in day-to- day life?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• describe the physical properties of metals
• describe the composition of alloys
• identify the uses of metals and alloys in day-to-day life
• explain the effects of rusting of metals

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.
